description: The pie chart presents the domain distribution of an annotated test set across 12 categories, with each slice labeled by domain name and percentage via external callouts connected by leader lines (no separate legend is shown, and no slice appears exploded or otherwise emphasized). The slices include AI/NLP Research in blue at about 24.3%, Econ. & Fin. in teal at about 18.4%, History in yellow at about 8.2%, Game&Anime in orange at about 8.2%, Daily Life in light cyan at about 7.1%, Med & Health in green at about 6.7%, Science in light blue at about 6.7%, Business in red at about 5.9%, Pet & Animal in light orange at about 5.5%, Law in pink at about 5.1%, Geography in yellow-gold at about 2.7%, and Math in dark green at about 1.2%; the slices do not appear to be arranged strictly in descending order around the circle.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the domain distribution of the annotated AttrEval-GenSearch test set, encompassing twelve distinct categories. The largest category, 'AI/NLP Research,' accounts for approximately 24.3% of the dataset, followed by 'Econ. & Fin.' at 18.4%. 'History' and 'Game&Anime' are tied at 8.2%, while 'Daily Life' constitutes 7.1%. 'Med & Health' and 'Science' both represent 6.7%, with 'Business' slightly lower at 5.9%. 'Pet & Animal' and 'Law' are close in proportion, at 5.5% and 5.1%, respectively. 'Geography' and 'Math' are the smallest categories, with 'Geography' at 3.7% and 'Math' at 2.2%. Notably, 'Daily Life' has shown a consistent increase in representation compared to previous datasets, while 'Geography' has seen a slight decline.
